title: Open Barrier Membrane Technique for the Treatment of Oroantral Communications: Two Case Reports
authors: Yotsova RV, Papanchev GY, Ali M, Gerova -Vatsova T. Cureus. 2024 Jul 4;16(7):e63854. doi: 10.7759/cureus.63854. * collacone®
supports: Clinical study from the botiss collacone / collafleece (collagen cone and fleece) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Abstract, verbatim (no separate conclusion section): “Oroantral communications (OACs) are relatively common complications after extractions of maxillary posterior teeth. Some defects can heal spontaneously, while others require surgical treatment. The lack of an appropriate therapeutic approach can lead to the epithelialization of the OAC that causes a permanent connection between the two cavities, called an oroantral fistula (OAF), and subsequent chronic sinusitis. Various treatment modalities have been used in cases of OACs, including advancement flaps, bone grafts, synthetic materials, and barrier membranes. We present two cases of closure of OACs with dense polytetrafluoroethylene (d-PTFE) membranes (of FDI tooth #28 in the first case and #17 in the second case), which were left exposed to the oral cavity. In both cases, healing was uneventful.” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
